knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A chip that cleaning cannot fix is recorded and reported. Filling or hiding it is not part of the cleaner's role.
A useful report states the facts: what, where, how big, whether it is safe, and whether the room can be used.
Keeping people away and not touching the item, then raising an urgent report, is the correct response to a possible electrical hazard.

practicalCriteria: Writes a factual report for a seeded fault that includes room, time, location, description and whether the room can be used.
Identifies a seeded hazard, stops work on it, and raises an urgent report under the emergency procedure, as observed.
Separates a seeded cleanable mark from a seeded fault and deals with the first without reporting it as a fault.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 percent pass mark (all three correct). Practical criteria are observed and signed off separately by an assessor. A knowledge pass is not practical competence.
evidenceRequired: Damage or maintenance report for the seeded fault
stopWorkCriteria: Repair attempted on a fault outside the cleaner's authority
